evidence:
**No blocking findings in this private independent whole-branch review.** The newly executed October 9 mutation evidence closes the previous P2 evidence finding. I found no additional blocking production-code defect in the complete examined delta.

Reviewed SHA: `3fea0704db8a951b3aff7db00551240b8cc4eb58`  
Tree: `f95f5a51daa0b46092eb0d2d4696dabdcb38adf7`  
Integration base: `70f5cd5453c167610571b883ef807fd5b593f843`

The checkout matched those values and Git status was empty at initial and final inspection. I remained read-only and offline. I ran no tests, mutations, installs, network calls, subagents, repairs, ref changes, verdict recording, publication or Anthropic calls. In-memory reconstruction of recorded diffs was evidence analysis, not proof execution.

I inspected all 18 changed files: runtime routing, runtime configuration, Settings diagnostics, cloud fallback policy, supervisor-status parsing, health probing, System Diagnostic UI, all seven added test files, the package script, targeted overrides and validation documentation. I read `AGENTS.md`, `.codex/agents/independent-reviewer.toml`, the approved supervisor design, surrounding main and Settings startup/secret call sites, Tauri bridge behavior, and native status/restart contracts. Inherited PR A/native behavior was treated as context rather than attributed to this PR B delta.

The former evidence finding is closed with high confidence. Its location was the historical mutation-proof section of `docs/validation/R4-BUG-004-RENDERER-ROUTING.md`, where the original 18-row table lacked independently auditable raw applied-diff/RED/restore records. The current evidence supplies newly executed equivalents at the frozen SHA; it does not retrospectively attest the September 29 runs.

I independently reconstructed **every one of the 39 applied mutation diffs** from the frozen Git source in memory. For every application:

- Removed and context lines matched the frozen source.
- Reconstructed mutated SHA-256 and Git blob ID matched the recorded mutation and diff index.
- Actual diff and TAP bytes matched their recorded SHA-256 values.
- Raw failing test names matched the manifest.
- Recorded failure diagnostics appeared in the raw TAP and contained `ERR_ASSERTION`.
- The restore record matched the corresponding manifest entry, named the frozen baseline, recorded clean-before/clean-after state, and restored the frozen source hash.

All **34 original named behavior tests** have matching raw assertion RED evidence. The coverage comprises 38 unique variants in 39 applications, with H11 and H11R applying the same mutation through different execution paths. All 18 historical table rows have current equivalents; S01–S20 cover additional assertions. Assertions and fixtures were not weakened. S16 changes only the scanner helper inside its test module.

Where npm executed both phases, those totals combine separately recorded source and runtime count lines. They are not a claim that the runtime phase executed when a source guard stopped the command.

H11’s actual failure was the existing OpenAQ local-only source assertion. The initial harness stopped after that valid RED because it expected the health runtime name; restoration was recorded. H11R preserves that earlier result and separately demonstrates the same mutation against direct mocked runtime tests, including the existing “local health and local-* targets never fall back” assertion. S20 similarly uses direct runtime execution. These distinctions are accurately disclosed.

Raw full-routing baselines before and after the new proofs both contain:

```text
# pass 10
# fail 0
# pass 56
# fail 0
```

The direct routing baseline contains:

```text
# pass 19
# fail 0
```

Their raw log hashes matched the manifest. The independently supplied derived audit agrees with my reconstruction.

The repaired stale-health-port behavior is correct in the inspected execution path. Connection failures invalidate the cached port before local-only requests rethrow. Caller cancellation exits before invalidation. HTTP responses retain their existing behavior. The replacement-port regression uses the real renderer cache/resolver and deferred mocked IPC, requiring the next health request to await confirmation of the replacement port without an unrelated request or manual invalidation.

Confirmed-port routing caches valid native confirmations, shares concurrent polling, and returns null without confirmation. Local requests use the port resolved for that request. A 401 invalidates and re-resolves before its single refreshed-token retry. Secret sync, validation and Settings diagnostics resolve a confirmed base and guard absent confirmation. The display/default-port helper remains outside these secret-bearing paths.

Cloud fallback eligibility matches the approved policy: connection failures and 5xx are eligible; 4xx and caller cancellation are excluded. Personal and unknown query parameters, bodies and unsupported methods remain local. Recognized coordinates are rounded, high-precision coordinate paths are blocked, and local-only health/diagnostic/secret endpoints cannot use cloud fallback. Cloud requests require a remote base and cloud key and strip Authorization.

Native payload names match the status parser. Malformed payloads are rejected rather than guessed. Supervisor explanations replace failed-probe reasons only for restarting/stopped phases, scheduled follow-up probing is bounded by the pending flag, displayed text is escaped, and restart eligibility is restricted to stopped state. Package and override changes are additive, with no new dependency or weakened existing test apparent in the delta.

I inspected saved full-gate execution evidence rather than rerunning it. The raw gate log SHA-256 matches `24ca89d6b76f0631592703eb5bca3d554d0da8bff8734b7c2ee110d0be684b02`, and the associated record identifies the exact frozen SHA/tree. Its actual outputs include routing 10/0 plus 56/0, supervisor 7/0, attribution 30/0, `Secret scan passed for 4987 file(s).`, and `Agentic validation gate passed.` Lockfile, lint, typechecks, cross-agent diagnostic, documentation, roadmap and build execution are recorded, with nonfatal build warnings retained. A successful diagnostic gate does not itself establish a publication verdict.

The frozen child changes only documentation relative to code-proof commit `000d0a8080acdde05fd86d5c4226bdb19e81e635`. I inspected both earlier repair mutation diffs and the M2 raw assertion showing expected zero invalidations versus actual one, with 18/1 counts. An attempted read of the older M1 TAP stalled without output, so I do not claim fresh complete raw M1 verification in this review. The fresh H/S evidence was fully accessible and independently audited; this read limitation does not reopen the original behavior-proof gap.

I read the full genuine scoped Sonnet review. Its conclusion, “No blocking findings in the scoped Codex repair,” covers the four-file repair only. Metadata identifies `claude-sonnet-4-6` for substantive review messages and records accepted `--effort medium`; service-side effort is not independently attested. Aggregate usage additionally reports Haiku with 39,609 input and 21 output tokens of undisclosed purpose. No Haiku review text or Opus usage is reported. The CLI succeeded; the wrapper’s subsequent all-usage-models-must-be-Sonnet assertion was self-imposed. I do not characterize that session as exclusively Sonnet or expand its conclusion into whole-branch approval.

Remaining limits are explicit: no installed-app, real Keychain, live sidecar/cloud, DOM restart-button execution, or force-quit/World Monitor acceptance was verified. Source secret-boundary proofs establish source wiring, not live secret execution. The bounded historical search did not recover the September 29 raw bundle; its timed-out broader search does not prove that bundle never existed. Current cloud deployment state was not independently checked.

No further evidence or code repair is required for the examined private whole-branch review conclusion. Manual acceptance remains outstanding. This review selects no publication route and authorizes no repository verdict: publishing the private `codex/pr1759-local-port-recovery` branch would still require whole-branch Sonnet review under the repository’s branch policy.
